full_judgment:
8. Mr. M.A. Wahab, the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioner submitted that the Court of appeal below committed an error of law apparent on the face of the records by observing that "it cannot be concluded that the title and interest of the land remained with the recorded persons simply because the land was recorded in their names at the time of C.S. operation" which is a clear violation of the provision of Section 103 B(5) of the Bengal Tenancy Act. He further added that the appellate Court below committed an error of law in holding that "the Kabuliyat Ext.2 and 2(a) sufficiently proved that Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired interest in the "Ka" and "Kha" schedule lands respectively" in view of the fact that there is no iota of evidence either in the plaint or in the deposition of the witnesses of the plaintiffs that Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi ever acquired the disputed land from the admitted recorded tenants Derajtullah Biswas and Herajtulalh Biswas rather it is on the record that the "Ka" schedule land originally belonged to Satkori Mitra and Hemlal Mitra which is all together a wrong,false and baseless in view of the Exts.3(d) and 3(e). He further submitted that the Court of appeal below committee an error of law by giving importance and reliance upon the Kabuliyat Exts.2 and 2(a) which have not been legally and properly proved by the plaintiff in this case. He further submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law in holding that "Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired interest in the land of C.S Khatian No.47 and C.S Khatian No.207," in fact that there is no evidence to that effect that both of them took settlement of the said "Ka" and "Kha" schedule lands respectively from the original owner. He added that the appellate Court also committed an error of law in placing reliance upon the S.A. record in respect of the non-disputed land. He further submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law by misreading the deposition of witnesses, particularly the deposition of the D.Ws. 2 and 3. He further submitted that the appellate Court also committed an error of law in not considering the evidence of P.W.1 Abdus Salam who has admitted the possession of the defendant No.1 in the disputed Plot Nos.50 and 52 by deposing that the distance between the homestead of the plaintiffs and the defendants No.1 Soleman is one bighat only, where in the defendant No.1 has admittedly been resided with his family in his ancestral homestead situated in the same Plot. In such view of the evidence the appellate Court erred in law in not holding that the defendants are in possession of the suit land. He further submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law in placing importance and relying upon the Dhakilas Ext.1-series which have not been proved in accordance with law and the procedure. He further submitted that Ext.1 series are not genuine, rather forged, fraudulent and created for the purpose of the suit. But the appellate Court below committed an error of law on relying upon the Dhakilas Ext.1- series and as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. He also submitted that the appellate Court committed an error of law. in not considering the petition filed by the respondent No.1 stating that the respondent No.2 died on 7.10.1980 and the appeal was abated as the heir/heirs of respondent No.2 Chandra Bibi was not made party in time. He added that the plaintiffs must prove his own case and weaknesses of the defence case, the plaintiff will not be entitled to get any benefit. According to him the' plaintiff failed to prove the case resulting which the trial Court dismissed the suit. But the appellate Court below without controverting the findings of the trial Court on misreading the evidence, misconstrued the documents, thus, mere surmise and conjecture allowed the appeal. He also referred the evidence of D.Ws. and submitted that from which it is apparent that the appellate court committed error of law, and as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set aside. 

 10. Having gone though the impugned judgment it appears that the appellate Court opined "that the plaintiffs have produced certified copy of the Kabuliyat dated 05.2.1937 Ext.2 and the certified copy of the Kabuliyat dated 24.6.1950 Ext.2(a) to show that Ayejudiin Biswas acquired C.S. Plot Nos.50 and 52 appertaining to C.S. Khatian No.47 and Chandra Bibi became owner of the entire land of C.S. Khatian No.207. The Kabuliyat Ext.2 was executed about 45 years back and Kabuliyat Ext.2(a) was executed more than 30 years back, so in my opinion that those old documents should be given due importance. It has been argued on behalf of the defendant-respondent that the plaintiff could not produce any document to show as to how Ayejudiin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired their interest in the suit Plots. It is true that the plaintiffs have not produced any documents regarding the title of Ayejuddin Biswas in "Ka" schedule land and Chandra Bibi in respect of "Kha" schedule land. I think the Kabuliyat Ext.2 and 2(a) sufficiently proved that Ayejuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi acquired interest in the "Ka" and "Kha" schedule land respectively. If Ayejuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi had no interest in the said property, there was no reason why Abdul Karim (since dead) would execute Kabuliyat in their favour." After appreciating the materials on record I am of the view that the above findings neither correct nor based on material evidence on record. Further this court is of the view that while C.S. record of rights admittedly stands in the name of the predecessor of the plaintiff and defendants by executing Kabuliyat one of them i.e. by plaintiff, surely no right, title will create by such Kabuliyat either in favour of Kabuliyat giver and receiver. Kabuliyat receiver, or giver must proved that he had right, title and interest over suit property. In the instant case although Kabuliyat receiver was examined by the plaintiff as P.W. but he failed to produce any documentary evidence in his favour showing that he was the real owner of the suit khatian by any documentary evidence in other capacity, and as such, far away to admit the alleged Kabuliyat as his title. I am of the view that a unilateral Kabuliyat does not confer the title either parties without basis of proof of any documentary evidence. 

 13. The trial Court while dismissed the suit clearly opined that P.W3 claimed to be the son of Chandra Bibi and he deposes that his mother got the suit land by way of auction purchase, but no such paper has been connected or submitted before the any Courts. The trial Court also found that both in C.S. and S.A. Porcha of the suit land were not recorded in the name of Chandra Bibi. Only in S.A. Porcha of Khatian No.269 her name was included in equal share with the name of the father of the plaintiff and defendants. 

 Apart from those documentary evidence it is further crystal clear from the oral and documentary evidence of the P,Ws that the Ayezuddin Biswas and Chandra Bibi had no documentary evidence on which basis the title of late Abdul Karim can be conferred in his favour. On the other hand according to the provisions of section 103 B of the Bengal Tenancy. Act, 1885 the record of rights published in the name of tenant shall be conclusive proof of such Publication from which it is proved beyond all reasonable doubts that predecessor of Late Abdul Karim and Late Abdul Jalil were the real owner of the suit Khatian as per C.S. record of rights which never became unworthy by any other documentary evidence.
